rows.text: # Evolution: evidences, adaptive radiation, Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, human evolution ## 1. Introduction Opening frame for **Evolution** — what the topic is, why it matters, a real-world hook (Nepal where possible), the map of what follows, and the learning outcomes (biology-plan.md §3.1, block I). Prose depth is written in the Heredity and Evolution fill pass. ## 2.…  ·  Darwin's 1859 theory — descent with modification by natural selection — is supported by evidence from every branch of biology. Population genetics later gave it a mathematical spine: the **Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium** defines the genetic baseline of a population that is NOT evolving, so any deviation names the evolutionary force at work.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Evidences list: palaeontology (fossils), comparative anatomy (homologous/analogous organs), embryology (Haeckel), molecular (cytochrome c), biogeography — five with one line each.  ·  Trick 2: Hardy–Weinberg: p² + 2pq + q² = 1 — p² = AA, 2pq = Aa, q² = aa; disturbed by mutation, migration, drift, selection, non-random mating — the five forces.

rows.text: Trick 3: Adaptive radiation: Darwin's finches (beaks), Australian marsupials — one ancestor → many niches; convergent evolution is the analogous-organ flip side.  ·  Trick 4: Human evolution order: Australopithecus → Homo habilis → H. erectus → Neanderthal → H. sapiens — brain size increases, jaw decreases.  ·  define + example each sub-idea: evolution, evidences, adaptive radiation, hardy-weinberg equilibrium.
